title: Client Transition Orchestrator and Compatibility Canary Guide
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Define an orchestrated, low-friction path for client SDKs and API consumers to migrate across behavioral changes tied to streaming, tool/function calling, and structured output evolutions. Provide a repeatable canary + replay strategy, clear behavior-flag semantics, and migration artifacts to avoid regressions and customer breakage.
motivation: Recent model and runtime changes require behavioral flags and compatibility shims for streaming chunking, tool invocation payloads, and structured-output schemas. We need a standardized migration orchestration so customers can opt into new behavior gradually, fail safely, and get automated compatibility test-feedback during rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A documented orchestrator runbook that defines the canary phases, metrics, and rollback thresholds
Behavior flags (opt-in and opt-out) with SDK defaults and server-side gating documented
Automated replay harness that can validate N historical requests across old/new variants without exposing customer data
Client migration guides for streaming, tool calling, and structured outputs published in docs with sample code
Regression detection alerting configured in Console with dashboards and a runbook for oncall
One internal pilot with two customer integrations completed and lessons captured
implementation_notes: Create a 'canary orchestration' workflow in the release subsystem that can target specific client cohorts by API key, region, and traffic percentile
Expose three behavior flags for each major surface: streaming_chunked_mode, toolcall_strict_params, structured_output_schema_v2
Default behavior: new behavior off for GA-breaking changes. Use staged opt-in for early adopters via API key tagging
Provide SDK helpers to detect and log inconsistencies between local parsing and server response schemas
Add a replay adapter that redacts PII and replays requests to new candidate variants in an isolated environment
test_plan: Unit + integration tests for behavior flags at SDK and server layer
Synthetic fuzz suite for streaming boundary cases (partial frames, dropped connections) against both old/new modes
Replay-based regression suite: sample 100k requests from production traffic (redacted) and compare structured outputs and toolcall side-effects
Canary smoke checks: latency, token error rate, parsed-toolcall success rate, structured-output schema validation rate
Golden prompt set evals to surface subtle semantic regressions introduced by model/runtime changes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal: run orchestration on internal API keys and CI traffic. Duration: 48h. Goal: no schema regressions
Phase 1 - Early adopters: invite customers on early-access list, enable behavior flags per-customer. Duration: 1 week. Metrics: parse success >= 99%, no increased error rate
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: enable for 5%/25%/50% traffic slices by API key cohorts with automatic rollback on SLO breaches
Phase 3 - Opt-in sunset window: announce deprecation of legacy behavior, keep legacy on for remaining users for a 90-day grace period
Emergency rollback: server-side kill switch that reverts routing to legacy model/variant within 2 minutes
communication_plan: Pre-announcement to customers in affected cohorts with migration checklist and SDK upgrade notes
Public docs page with a 'What changed' matrix mapping old->new payload and error codes
In-console banner for affected API keys during canary phases with direct link to migration guide
Weekly status updates to customers in early adopter cohort and a final deprecation notice 30 days before mandatory switch
migration_artifacts: Client migration guide: examples for Node/Python/Go showing streaming parser changes
Server-side sample adapters for toolcall translation and backward compatibility shim
Schema diff tool output for structured outputs (old vs v2) with suggested normalization snippets
Prebuilt redaction and replay tool for engineering to run compatibility test suites
monitoring_and_alerting: New per-route metrics: parsing_error_rate, toolcall_mismatch_rate, structured_schema_failures
SLO watch: 99.9th percentile latency and 99.5% success rate for tool invocation parsing
Automated anomaly detection to flag semantic regressions derived from eval-run comparisons
Incident runbook that ties alerts to rollback and postmortem actions
risks: Customers with brittle parsing/readers may break despite canary — mitigation: longer grace window and client SDK parsing helpers
Replay may miss edge cases due to incomplete telemetry — mitigation: expand golden prompt set and include synthetic edge cases
False positives in regression detectors could trigger unnecessary rollbacks — mitigation: require multi-signal confirmation before auto-rollback
Operational complexity of per-key routing increases attack surface for misconfiguration — mitigation: additional preflight checks and audit logs
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting completed. Agreed on three primary behavior flags and draft canary phases.

2025-02-25: Security signoff checklist reviewed; replay redaction requirements added to scope.

notes: This ticket is the PM-led orchestration and documentation effort. Engineering tasks will be tracked in sub-issues created under ENG-* keys and linked in dependencies. Keep the communications conservative for enterprise customers to avoid accidental opt-ins.
